title: Residue units and prime coordinates of a supported complete toric cover
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively, whose only invertible element is $0$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Put $G=P^{\rm gp}$. Let $n\ge0$. For a local coefficient ring $L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be the completion of $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Consider either a field $L=k$ with $R=B_k(P,n)$, or a Cohen ring $L=C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with $R=B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$, where $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In either case $z^q$ denotes the image of the chart monomial in $R$. Let $r\ge0$ and let $\lambda:G\hookrightarrow\mathbf Z^r$ be an injective group homomorphism with $\lambda(P)=\lambda(G)\cap\mathbf N^r$. Put $M=\lambda(G)$, $B=B_L(P,n)$ and $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Suppose $\iota:B\hookrightarrow A$ identifies $B$ with the series supported on $(M\cap\mathbf N^r)\times\mathbf N^n$ via $z^q\mapsto X^{\lambda(q)}$, and $\rho:A\to B$ is deletion of coefficients outside that support, read through $\iota^{-1}$. In the field case put $D=A$; in the Cohen case put $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$ and $D=A/(\Theta)$. Suppose the induced inclusion $R\hookrightarrow D$ and the $R$-linear retraction $\bar\rho:D\to R$ are given by these maps (so in the Cohen case $\bar\rho([a])=[\rho(a)]$). Then $B$, $R$ and $D$ are local rings with common residue field $L/\mathfrak m_L$, and their residue maps are induced by the constant coefficient followed by $L\to L/\mathfrak m_L$. An element of each ring is a unit if and only if its residue is nonzero; the map $\bar\rho$ preserves residue and sends every unit of $D$ to a unit of $R$. Moreover $D$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For $1\le i\le r$ the coordinate images $X_i\in D$ are nonzero prime nonunits, and the ideals $(X_i)D$ are distinct height-one prime ideals. Here a prime element means a nonzero nonunit dividing one factor whenever it divides a product; height one means nonzero with no prime strictly between the ideal and $(0)$. No perfection of the Cohen residue field is assumed, and $r=0$ and $n=0$ are included.

source.place: ILO Expose VI 1.4 and 1.6(i)--(ii), printed pp. 69--70, supplies context and the complete local model presentations only. proof.text: Write $d=r+n$, $\kappa=L/\mathfrak m_L$ and $\epsilon:A\to L$ for constant coefficient. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables], $\epsilon$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. Each $z^q$ for $q\ne0$ maps to a nonconstant monomial: integrality embeds $P$ in $G$, and injectivity of $\lambda$ implies $\lambda(q)\ne0$. Thus in the Cohen case $\epsilon(\Theta)=p$. Apply [lem-trf-power-series-cohen-hypersurface-normality] with these $d$ variables: in the field case it gives that $D=A$ is regular local and a normal domain; in the Cohen case it gives the same for $D=A/(\Theta)$, since the constant coefficient is exactly $p$. Regular local rings are Noetherian by the definition included in that cited statement. Independently [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] gives that $A$ is local and that its nonunits are exactly $\ker(A\xrightarrow{\epsilon}L\to\kappa)$.

source.place: Tags 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM); agent assembly for the stipulated supported inclusion

proof.text: Identify $B$ with the stipulated supported subring and restrict $\epsilon$ to it. Constants belong to its support, so its residue map onto $\kappa$ is surjective. If $b\in B$ has nonzero residue, its constant coefficient $c$ is a unit of the local ring $L$. Put $h=c^{-1}b-1$, which has zero constant coefficient and the same allowed support $H=(M\cap\mathbf N^r)\times\mathbf N^n$. The formal series $g=c^{-1}\sum_{j\ge0}(-h)^j$ is defined coefficientwise: a coefficient of total degree $a$ receives terms only for $j\le a$, with finitely many decompositions in each product, by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Since $0\in H$ and $H+H\subseteq H$, every term and hence $g$ has support in $H$, so $g\in B$. The finite geometric identity in each degree gives $bg=1$. Conversely a unit of $B$ maps to a unit in the field $\kappa$, hence has nonzero residue. Therefore the kernel of this residue map is precisely the nonunits; it is a proper maximal ideal containing every proper ideal, so $B$ is local with residue field $\kappa$.

source.place: Agent coefficientwise geometric-series calculation; multiplication as in Tag 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series), supported local model of ILO VI 1.6

proof.text: In the field case $R=B$ and $D=A$, so the preceding steps already prove the residue and unit assertions. In the Cohen case the constant coefficient of $\theta$ is $p$ (read through the supported inclusion), so $(\theta)$ lies in the kernel of the residue map of $B$; likewise $(\Theta)$ lies in the residue kernel of $A$. Both residue maps therefore descend to surjections $R\to\kappa$ and $D\to\kappa$. A quotient class with nonzero residue has a representative with nonzero residue, which is a unit in $B$, respectively $A$, by steps 1--2; its inverse descends. A class with zero residue cannot be a unit because its image in the nonzero field $\kappa$ is zero. Thus the nonunits in either quotient form exactly the kernel of its residue map, making each quotient local with residue field $\kappa$. This argument also specifies the residue maps as constant coefficient followed by reduction, independently of the chosen representative.

source.place: Agent elementary quotient calculation for the complete local models in ILO VI 1.6(ii); maximal ideals as in Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary)

proof.text: The zero exponent belongs to $H$, so deleting coefficients outside $H$ never changes the constant coefficient. Hence $\rho$ preserves constant coefficient and $\bar\rho$ preserves residue. In the Cohen case this follows on representatives from the assumed formula $\bar\rho([a])=[\rho(a)]$, using the well-defined residue maps of step 3. If $u\in D$ is a unit, its residue is nonzero by step 3, and $\bar\rho(u)$ has the same nonzero residue, so is a unit of $R$ by that step. No multiplicativity of $\rho$ or $\bar\rho$ is used.

proof.text: Fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Permuting the variables and applying [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] gives a surjection $A\to A_i=L[[X_1,\ldots,\widehat X_i,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ with kernel $(X_i)$, by setting $X_i=0$. In the field case $D/(X_i)\cong A_i$. In the Cohen case let $\Theta_i$ be the image of $\Theta$; then $D/(X_i)\cong A_i/(\Theta_i)$. Explicitly both quotients of $A$ have kernel $(\Theta,X_i)$: if the image of $a$ is $\Theta_i b_i$, lift $b_i$ to $b\in A$ and then $a-\Theta b\in(X_i)$. Constant coefficient of $\Theta_i$ is still exactly $p$. Applying [lem-trf-power-series-cohen-hypersurface-normality] in $d-1$ variables, in either case, makes this quotient a nonzero domain. Consequently $(X_i)D$ is a proper prime ideal, so $X_i$ is a nonunit and divides one of $a,b$ whenever it divides $ab$.

proof.text: The Noetherian domain $D$ from step 1 has prime ideal $(0)$. For each $i$, the prime ideal $(X_i)D$ is minimal over the principal ideal generated by $X_i$, since it equals that ideal. The principal ideal theorem [lem-sfb-krull-principal-ideal-height-bound] gives height at most one. Step 6 gives the strict chain $(0)\subsetneq(X_i)D$, hence height exactly one and no intermediate prime, as required. If $r=0$ the coordinate assertions are empty. All the preceding calculations allow $n=0$; when $r+n=0$ the series rings are their coefficient rings by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and the Cohen quotients are $C/pC$. No step assumes perfection of the residue field.

There are no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the base copy (checked against the Q137 de7c snapshot). No SGA is used. Source: ILO VI 1.6(i)-(ii) (PDF pp. 75-76) gives the local models k[[P]][[t]] and C(k)[[P]][[t]]/(f) with f congruent to p mod (P-{0}, t). The item attributes no theorem to ILO. Step 1: the constant coefficient of Theta is p, because lambda is injective with lambda(P) in N^r, so z^q for q nonzero goes to a nonconstant monomial. The normality node's hypotheses (C Cohen with maximal ideal pC, constant coefficient exactly p) are checked, and Noetherianity comes from def-weil-regular-scheme. Step 2: the supported geometric inverse is coefficientwise finite and stays in the support H because 0 is in H and H+H is in H. Since iota(B) is all series supported on H, the inverse lies in B, and B is local. Step 3: the quotient residue criterion. Step 4: rho keeps the exponent-0 coefficient. Step 5: I checked the kernel argument (Theta, X_i) and that pi preserves the constant coefficient; the normality node is then applied in d-1 variables. Step 6: the coefficient comparison gives a_0 = 0 and then 1 = p*a_{e_Y}, a contradiction, so the X_i are nonzero and pairwise distinct. Step 7: the Krull leaf plus the chain from (0) gives height one. Edge cases checked: r=0, r+n=0 (C/pC), theta = p+X_1, theta = p+X_1X_2, and P={0} with r>0. The parent lem-trf-complete-toric-boundary-class-injectivity step 1 uses exactly these conclusions.
